subject: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment - hardware & offline ops follow-up
messages:

Subject: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment - hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi James / Sophia —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-up items so we can align the next steps for the on-prem, air-gapped deployment: 

Summary from our call:
- Deployment mode: fully air-gapped Private (on-prem) with no egress from the protected network.
- Initial workload: inference for customer support and transaction monitoring (mixed chat + embeddings).
- Target throughput: ~4000 tokens/sec steady across peak windows; burst capacity expected for month-end reporting.

Questions / asks (so we can size hardware and plan offline ops):
1) Hardware preference: do you have a preferred vendor/CPU/GPU spec? From our side we typically recommend NVIDIA A100 80GB (or equivalent Ampere/Blackwell family) — targeting 6-8 GPUs for initial cluster depending on concurrency.
2) Maintenance / offline windows: what windows are available for OS/kernel/firmware maintenance (weekly, monthly, quarterly)?
3) Procurement: will Legacy Bank source the servers and network, or would you prefer Redwood's hardware partners to provide a quote?

Attachments: Ive attached our on-prem hardware guidelines and an installation checklist to help with procurement and operations planning. Also attaching a short SOC2 summary you can share with procurement.

Next steps I propose: 
- Ben to follow up with pricing & purchase vs. bring-your-own options.
- Dev to provide detailed offline upgrade/patching procedure and image signing flow.
- Schedule a technical deep dive with your infra & security teams next week (30-45m).

Available times (Pacific): Tue 10/24 9-11am, Wed 10/25 1-4pm. Let me know which works.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Hardware & vendor: We prefer to keep procurement in-house where possible. Our current on-prem pockets are Dell PowerEdge with AMD CPUs and a mix of NVIDIA H100s in a separate cluster. We would prefer to avoid new vendor lock-in unless necessary. Will Redwood support cross-vendor configurations (i.e., mixed CPU vendor + NVIDIA GPUs)?

2) Maintenance windows: For the secured environment we have a monthly 4-hour maintenance window (first Sunday of month 02:00-06:00 local). For critical patches we can schedule additional ad-hoc windows with advanced notice.

3) Offline upgrades & support: We will need a clear offline upgrade path — can you confirm if Redwood supports image bundles and signed updates delivered via USB/sneakernet? Also want to understand support SLAs for air-gapped installs (onsite vs remote).

Please also send the full SOC2 report (or a redacted version) to procurement; the attached summary is a start but procurement will ask for evidence.

Happy to meet Wed 10/25 1-2pm PT for the technical session. Adding Procurement contact on the next email.

—James O'Neil
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Legacy Bank
j.oneil@legacybank.com | (212) 555-0199

Subject: RE: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment - hardware & offline ops follow-up

James — appreciate the context. Short answers and proposal: 

- Mixed CPU vendors: Yes — Redwood's runtime is vendor-agnostic for CPUs. The key requirement is supported NVIDIA drivers and a compatible CUDA/ORC stack on the nodes that will run GPUs. H100 / A100 are both supported; we’ll validate driver/HCX combos during the onboarding checklist.

- Sizing recommendation (initial): 6x NVIDIA H100 80GB (for production inference + KV cache) + 2x management nodes (no GPUs) — or 8x A100 80GB as an alternative if H100 procurement is constrained. We’ll run an initial perf estimate after you share expected concurrency/avg sequence length.

- Procurement options:
  1) BYO hardware: Legacy Bank sources servers; Redwood provides the installation images, signed update bundles, and step-by-step ops runbook.
  2) Partner procurement: Redwood can coordinate a quote from our hardware partners (lead time ~6-8 weeks).

- Pricing signals: Private deployment (customer-managed infra) is a platform license + per-node support fee. I’ll send a formal quote after we agree on sizing and procurement path.

Next steps: Confirm Wed 10/25 1-2pm PT for the technical deep dive. Marissa, can you lock it? I’ll prepare a short slide with pricing ranges and licensing options.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment - hardware & offline ops follow-up

James — quick technical notes on the air-gapped upgrade & offline ops flow to address your questions: 

1) Image bundles & signing: Redwood provides signed OS + runtime image bundles. For air-gapped installs we support image ingestion via removable media (USB or mounted external drive). Each bundle includes SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest that the install agent verifies before applying.

2) Driver & firmware compatibility: We require validated NVIDIA driver versions for H100/A100 families; if your compute hosts have AMD CPUs that's fine as long as PCIe and firmware meet vendor minimums. We'll run a pre-install validation script (non-intrusive) during the technical call.

3) Offline patching cadence: We recommend monthly security patches and quarterly kernel/firmware updates for stable inference workloads. For critical CVEs we support ad-hoc signed hotfix bundles that can be applied during an approved maintenance window.

4) Node replacement & data persistence: Model KV caches are ephemeral; for node replacement we recommend draining traffic, preserving model artifacts on an internal artifact registry, and rehydrating caches post-replace. We will provide scripts for safe drain/rehydration.

5) Support model & escalation: For air-gapped deployments Redwood offers 24x7 phone+email support for critical incidents (SLA tiering available). Remote debugging will rely on customer-provided jump boxes / approved bastions; on-site engineering is available as paid add-on.

I attached the installation checklist and hardware guidelines referenced by Marissa. I’ll bring a short validation script to the call on Wed so we can run it live against a lab host if you have a staging node available.

—Dev Patel
